messages:
maya: Quick thread — ran a prefill+decode sweep across A100 vs H100 in us-west / eu-west / ap-southeast for Mistral-7B and Llama-7B. TL;DR: H100 wins tokens/sec on short seqs but we saw a prefill tail in eu-west that pushed p99 for H100 above A100 at high seqs. charts: https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/3398765432 :spiral_chart:

ana: Can you paste the numbers? short vs long seqs and the $/1M tokens?

maya: pasted csv snippet below (prefill+decode combined, tokens/sec and $/1M tokens at commit kernel v1.13):

```
model,region,gpu,seq,tokens_per_sec,ms_p50,ms_p99,dollars_per_1M
mistral-7b,us-west,a100,64,14.2,70,190,3.2
mistral-7b,us-west,h100,64,15.8,60,140,3.6
mistral-7b,eu-west,a100,1024,3.1,420,1350,9.5
mistral-7b,eu-west,h100,1024,2.7,480,1760,11.2
llama-7b,ap-southeast,a100,256,8.5,120,420,5.8
llama-7b,ap-southeast,h100,256,9.9,110,310,6.4
```
```
\nmaya: Notes: - H100 is better on short seqs (64/256) as expected. - Big gap on eu-west/1024: H100 has higher p99 and lower tokens/sec. No kernel OOMs, just thermal redispatch / fallthrough logs on the hosts.

leo: Interesting. Did the host show any PM telemetry or redispatch events?

maya: Yes — infra logs show scheduler fallthrough to slower kernels at the 1.5s mark during prefill for H100 machines. snippet from host log: ``[2026-07-09T17:04:12Z] kernel_selector: fallthrough -> kernel_v1_fallback latency=150ms reason=thermal_headroom``

sam: Could this be a driver/firmware mismatch? We recently rolled driver 525.x in eu-west for H100s.

ethan: I saw a similar thing last month when autoscaler bumped concurrency on H100s under sustained long-context workloads. It triggers a thermal governor that makes kernels pick conservative paths.

ana: Do we have kernel selection config? maybe the cost model prefers safe kernels for long seqs.

maya: Kernel selector config used: ``--kernel-policy=bandwidth_first --fallback=allow``. We also tried `compute_first` for one run and it reduced p99 by ~200ms but increased avg power draw and $/1M tokens by ~0.6.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolled host-firmware v2.8 to h100-cluster-eu-west at 3398765440. No restarts required. :white_check_mark:

leo: Thanks infra-bot. Suggestion: run a small A/B with `--kernel-policy=compute_first` and `--kernel-policy=bandwidth_first` with identical qparams (q4_0) and q8x4 to compare economic tradeoffs. Keep batch sizes fixed to 1 to isolate prefill cost.

maya: Agreed. I'll kick off 2x runs tonight across the three regions, q4_0 + q8x4, seqs 64/256/1024, and capture tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, and $/1M. I'll also capture host thermal telemetry and kernel decision traces.

sam: For $/1M we should normalize to on-demand list prices we use in dashboards and add a column for model-quality delta vs baseline (few-shot eval).

maya: Yup — adding quality checks. If quality regresses with q8x4 beyond threshold we'll mark it as blocked for rollout.

ethan: One more: check NVLINK topology variants in eu-west cluster. Some racks have mixed PCIE/NVLINK and that can affect KV cache performance under long context.

maya: noted. Will include topology tag in the run metadata.

ana: fwiw: if the fallback is thermal-driven we can try limiting sustained prefill rate via client-side pacing as a short-term mitigation for EU customers.

maya: Good fallback. I'll write a short runbook if the A/B confirms thermal fallthrough.

leo: awesome. ping me when results are up — would like to add a small note to the regional capacity sizing doc.

maya: will do. thanks all :rocket:
